summary: Radar as of 2026-10-09 06:00 UTC. Plague is still the only focus, and the official picture changed on Oct 8, so status pieces need rewriting. Russia's health watchdog (Rospotrebnadzor) and the regional governor say monitoring of all contacts is complete, nearly 5,000 lab samples found no dangerous pathogens, and they deny reports of a second sick employee (Reuters, The Moscow Times, Oct 8). WHO has said no cause of death is officially confirmed and that, based on unofficial information, the public health risk to the general population 'appears to be low'. On Oct 8 WHO head Tedros said WHO had asked Russia to respond to media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause (Al Jazeera). CDC says it has 'measures in place to identify and assess travelers arriving from the affected region'. About 200 travelers a year come from Irkutsk oblast, CDC calls the threat to the US 'extremely low', and there are no do-not-board orders (ABC, Axios, Washington Times). ABC's page dates the CDC statement 'Wednesday, October 8', but Wednesday was Oct 7, so check the date before publishing. Demand: Wikipedia's 'Plague (disease)' page is at about 11.8k views a day and newly in the top 1,000, and every major outlet has run a 'should I worry' explainer, so the generic explainer is now peaking. Best openings: dated status decoders, calm US-angle questions (CDC traveler checks, plague in US parks), what 'contacts completed observation' means, and the vaccine question (a scope-error trap, so handle with care). Snapshot topics on person-to-person spread and on symptoms remain the strongest steady performers. Reject all bioweapon, cover-up and permafrost speculation, plus the mother's 'I know the truth' coverage.

candidates.topic: Plague report in Russia, status as of Oct 8: Russia says contact checks are complete and nearly 5,000 samples found no dangerous pathogens. WHO says no cause of death has been officially confirmed.
candidates.angle: A dated three-column decoder: what Russian authorities say (Rospotrebnadzor and the regional governor, Oct 8), what WHO has said (cause not officially confirmed; risk to the general population 'appears to be low' based on unofficial information), and what is still open. Not confirmed is not the same as ruled out. Credit every line to the body that said it.
candidates.why_now: On Oct 8 Russia declared contact monitoring complete, while WHO is still asking for formal answers. That is a fresh status change on top of very heavy search interest (Wikipedia about 11.8k views a day). Search for 'latest' intent is high, and few creators date their status lines.

candidates.topic: Plague and US travel: CDC says it has measures in place to assess travelers from Irkutsk oblast, about 200 travelers a year, and calls the threat to the US 'extremely low'
candidates.angle: A calm, action-framed Short: 'Plague and Travel: What CDC Is Doing at US Airports'. Cover the official numbers, explain that a public health assessment is not a diagnosis, and note that there are no do-not-board orders. Add the CDC line that there has been no person-to-person spread in the US since 1924. Anyone with possible exposure should contact a doctor or local health authority urgently.
